clue.text: Degree to which I trace development of microorganisms

indicators.note: a development is a working-out into a new form, so the letters after it are rearranged

blocks.note: a Bachelor of Arts degree
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist measures how far they can follow the growth of a culture of germs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are single-celled microorganisms, so the plural noun is a straight synonym.

clue.text: It'll go with a bang — or else fail

blocks.note: first meaning: an explosive device
second meaning: to flop badly, as a show does

explanation.surface: Something will either make a splash or flop completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an explosive device and an informal verb for a show or venture that flops.

clue.text: Detain domestic after a student vanishes

indicators.note: something that vanishes is taken away, so those letters drop out of the longer word

blocks.note: domestic in the sense of home affairs, within a country
A taken as written, L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Someone holds a housekeeper back once a student goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: INTERNAL loses its last two letters, A and L, leaving INTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, especially an enemy national, during wartime, which is a form of detention.

clue.text: Tutor due freely to offer up thanks in church

indicators.note: done freely means done loosely, without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, going up means the word reads from bottom to top
one word goes inside the other, as a person sits in a building

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ta is informal British for thank you
Church of England

explanation.surface: A teacher willingly gives thanks during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach, so as a verb it is a synonym for educate.

clue.text: A French stick and a stone

blocks.note: first meaning: a long thin loaf of bread
second meaning: a gem cut as a small long rectangle

explanation.walkthrough: A French stick is the British name for the long loaf; a gem cut in a narrow rectangle shares the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the classic long French loaf and a narrow rectangular cut of gemstone.

clue.text: Holiday reading?

blocks.note: surface reading: a novel to enjoy on the beach
setter's reading: the small guide a traveller reads from to speak a foreign language abroad

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the reading is not for pleasure but for asking directions and ordering meals in another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller consults a pocket guide of useful foreign expressions on a trip abroad.

clue.text: Stop this bad weather

blocks.note: first meaning: halt, stay motionless
second meaning: a spell of frost and ice

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence it is a plea to end the cold snap; split, the command to halt and the icy spell are one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a command to stand still and a noun for a period of very cold, icy conditions.

clue.text: Dreamed about a river on a desert island

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word wraps round the letters given by the rest

blocks.note: to moon is to daydream idly
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A castaway lies daydreaming beside a river on a deserted island.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go in after the first letter of MOONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone marooned is stranded, the classic fate of a castaway left alone on an island.

clue.text: Hate a book taking three quarters of an hour

indicators.note: keeping three of four parts means one of the four letters is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
the four-letter word, of which three letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a book that takes forty-five minutes to get through.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUR loses its U to keep three of its four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to detest or loathe, so the verb is a strong synonym.

clue.text: Mad — on reflection — to have a try

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bats is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone concludes, after thinking it over, that it would be crazy to attempt something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab at something is an attempt, as in 'have a stab at it', an idiom for a try.

clue.text: Cheers as bottle goes in three different directions

indicators.note: the word that goes in is placed inside the letters around it

blocks.note: East, North and South, three compass points
bottle is British slang for nerve

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers as a bottle is thrown in three directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve or courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to urge and hearten them, so as a verb it is a synonym.

clue.text: Fearful at onset of cockcrow

indicators.note: the onset of something is its very beginning, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: only the opening letter of this word is kept
the end of the same word, read on its own: the raven is the largest bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened at the first crowing of a rooster at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockcrow' must be split into two words: cock gives its first letter and crow is replaced by a member of the crow family.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, lacking in courage, so it fits an adjective for being afraid.

clue.text: Offers made by charity workers

blocks.note: first meaning: puts forward freely, as a verb
second meaning: unpaid helpers

explanation.surface: Donations are made by people who work for a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for freely offering something and a noun for unpaid workers.

clue.text: Holding animal, man walked unsteadily

indicators.note: one word holding another keeps it inside, wrapped round it

blocks.note: a man's name, short for Edward
an example of an animal

explanation.surface: A man carrying an animal staggered under its weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to move shakily, as if about to fall, so the past tense matches a wobbly walk.

clue.text: Setting for a superior audience

blocks.note: surface reading: a venue for snobbish, refined spectators
setter's reading: superior means literally higher up, the spectators seated in the top tier of a theatre

explanation.walkthrough: Superior is used in its literal sense of higher, not grander: the cheapest seats are the highest ones.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the uppermost balcony of seats, far above the stalls, has this name.

clue.text: Telling made-up story during phone call

indicators.note: made-up means invented or concocted, so the letters are rearranged
one thing happening during another sits inside it

blocks.note: a ring is British informal for a phone call
a synonym, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies about a fiction while on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made-up story' reads as one idea, a lie, but made-up works on the word story alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating a story means recounting it, so the participle is a synonym for telling.

clue.text: Grace is late (nothing unusual)

blocks.note: late means dead, abbreviated DEC for deceased
zero, shaped like the letter O
rum is British informal for odd

explanation.surface: Arriving late with grace is a perfectly normal thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, a kind of grace or good manners.

clue.text: Insurrection at university on the increase

blocks.note: in British usage a student is up at university
a synonym

explanation.surface: Campus revolt grows as student protest mounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a rebellion by people against authority, the same as an insurrection.

clue.text: Explosive anger erupts as journalist returns

indicators.note: something that erupts is blown apart, so the letters scatter into a new order
returning means going back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Furious rage boils over when a reporter comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, so it is an explosive in the noun sense.

clue.text: Con man used Wilder's name

indicators.note: used as in worked over or exploited, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A fraudster passed himself off under the name of Wilder, perhaps Billy or Gene.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler cheats people out of money, which is exactly what a con man does.

clue.text: Importance of English invasion of the island

indicators.note: an invasion moves into a territory, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A history question asks why an English landing on an island mattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight in the sense of influence or significance, as in 'carries weight', means importance.

clue.text: Loafer's place of work

blocks.note: surface reading: where an idler does (or avoids) his job
setter's reading: a loafer is someone who makes loaves of bread

explanation.walkthrough: A loafer usually means an idler or a shoe; here it is coined for a maker of loaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaves are baked in a shop or workshop where bread is made, the baker's workplace.

clue.text: Bishop set to extend an opening

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to reach is to stretch out

explanation.surface: A bishop is about to widen a gap, or perhaps lengthen a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a gap or break, such as one made in a wall, so it is an opening.

clue.text: Amateur detective hired by French relative

blocks.note: Detective Inspector
let means rented out
French for aunt

explanation.surface: An unpaid sleuth has been taken on by a family member from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without serious commitment, much like a dabbling amateur.

clue.text: It's only fair

blocks.note: first meaning: merely, simply
second meaning: equitable, right

explanation.surface: A short remark that something is the reasonable thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only fair' reads as one phrase but splits into two meanings of a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning merely and an adjective meaning morally right or equitable.

clue.text: Jolts containers

blocks.note: first meaning: shakes or ..., as a verb
second meaning: glass pots with lids

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like someone shaking boxes; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for giving a sudden shock and a plural noun for glass vessels.

clue.text: Bird man has no right to come back

indicators.note: coming back is going the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a man is referred to as he
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man with a bird is not entitled to return.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Do certain plays without a belief system

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is left out
the letters play about, moving freely into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter that is taken out of the words before it

explanation.surface: Some dramas lack a coherent set of beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a set of principles taught and held by a church or party, a system of belief.
